title: Referendums & Direct Democracy
hook: Usually we elect others to decide for us. Sometimes the people decide a question themselves — that's direct democracy, and the referendum is its main modern tool.
key_points: Direct democracy lets citizens vote on policies themselves, not just choose representatives.
A referendum puts a specific question or law directly to a public vote.
An initiative lets citizens propose a measure and force a vote by gathering enough signatures.
It boosts legitimacy on big questions but can oversimplify complex issues into yes/no choices.
content_html: Most modern democracies are representative: citizens elect officials who then make decisions on their behalf. Direct democracy is the alternative impulse — letting the people decide particular questions themselves. Pure direct democracy, where everyone votes on everything, is impractical at the scale of a modern state, so it survives mainly through specific tools layered on top of representative government.
extra_html: The most common is the referendum: a vote that puts a single question or proposed law directly to the public, such as approving a constitutional amendment or a major treaty. A related device is the initiative, which lets citizens themselves propose a measure and compel a public vote by gathering a required number of signatures — shifting agenda-setting power from officials toward the public. Encyclopaedia Britannica notes these mechanisms vary widely in how binding and how frequent they are across countries. Their appeal is legitimacy: a decision made directly by voters carries unusual weight, and the option of a referendum can check representatives who drift from public opinion. The standard criticism is that reducing a complex, multi-sided issue to a single yes-or-no choice can oversimplify it, and that outcomes may turn on the wording of the question or the intensity of a campaign rather than careful deliberation.

related.title: What Democracy Means
related.hook: Rule by the people: a system where political power ultimately traces back to citizens, usually through regular, free elections.

related.title: How Votes Become Seats
related.hook: The same ballots can produce very different results depending on the electoral system used to count them.

related.title: Amending a Constitution
related.hook: A constitution has to last — but not freeze. Amendment rules let it change deliberately, usually demanding more agreement than an ordinary law.

flashcards.prompt: What is the difference between direct and representative democracy?
flashcards.back_html: In direct democracy citizens vote on policies themselves; in representative democracy they elect others to decide on their behalf.
